DUNCAN_NIGHT_REPORT_R01
CYCLE_ID = DNR01-20260830-008
SOURCE_WINDOW = 2026-08-30 / fresh cycle after accepted DNR01-20260830-007 and current archive head c802870ab96db7dc33e384fd9599a457527c3946
MAIN_HEAD_OBSERVED = b18ca6b9cce2dce6fe304ca8ae36c05df4f4dcb1
DAY_EVENTS_REVIEWED = issue:204 current restore entrypoint; issue:206 Night School/Fortress/admin hardening/product cycle 007 terminal evidence; issue:198 Tier-1 silhouette law; issue:199 character drawing + 4-6 controlled tone bands + sparse accents law; issue:202 pixel-QC-vs-latent-geometry boundary; PR:111 accepted DNR01-20260830-007 comment 5466429124; DUNCAN_CONTEXT_NEXT latest_cycle_id DNR01-20260830-007; Permanent Archive V1 head c802870ab96db7dc33e384fd9599a457527c3946
ANIME_TOPICS_STUDIED = anime color-accent hierarchy; chroma economy; preserving one focal color accent above restrained supporting masses; separating value hierarchy from chroma hierarchy; avoiding multiple equal-strength accents that compete for attention
OPEN_SOURCE_CODE_INSPECTED = OpenCV runtime 4.13.0; upstream opencv/opencv 4.x exact ref 755546643a671420fae0c20ec5d4cd24a228da8e dated 2026-08-29; Apache-2.0 contribution basis; modules/imgproc/src/color_lab.cpp RGB<->XYZ/Lab implementation with D65 matrices and spline/SIMD paths; modules/imgproc/test/test_color.cpp cvtColor forward/backward validation framework; cv2.cvtColor COLOR_RGB2Lab used; Python/NumPy only as existing numerical glue; no new framework/service
REFERENCE_PRINCIPLES = issue #199 requires 4-6 controlled tone bands followed by sparse accent darks/highlights and macro-over-micro discipline. This lesson extends that hierarchy into color: a focal chroma accent should remain perceptually distinct from restrained supporting masses without replacing silhouette/value structure. Reference-atlas principles transferred are controlled contrast and focal hierarchy only; no copyrighted frame, character, or exact style was copied.
EXERCISES = deterministic four-color synthetic anime palette in RGB: dark navy 28/30/38, cool mid 82/88/102, light neutral 176/168/158, focal red 220/48/58. OpenCV Lab chroma C*=sqrt(a^2+b^2): supporting masses 5.817/8.836/6.271 versus focal red 74.799. Focal chroma lead over second-highest = 65.963; minimum Lab Euclidean separation from focal to any supporting mass = 73.767. Muting focal red to 132/86/92 reduced chroma lead to 11.755 and minimum separation to 23.691. Adding a competing saturated blue 20/110/235 produced chroma values 73.375 and 74.799 for blue/red, collapsing top-vs-second focal uniqueness gap to 1.424.
VERIFICATION = fresh deterministic cv2 4.13.0 calculation using COLOR_RGB2Lab. Base focal red is the unique top-chroma mass with 65.963 C* lead. Muted focal retains rank but loses most separation. Competing saturated blue collapses unique-accent gap to 1.424, demonstrating that high saturation alone does not preserve a single focal hierarchy. Previous value-grouping regression replay with noisy DARK/MID/LIGHT synthetic composition and cv2.kmeans K=3 returned macro-IoU 1.000000 for all three semantic masses.
FAILURES = real Tier-1 production color transfer remains NOT PROVEN because no approved durable Tier-1 production raster/palette was available in the current public durable path for non-mutating analysis. CIE76-style Euclidean Lab distance is used here only as a bounded comparative metric, not a universal perceptual threshold. No claim that every ZORR frame must have exactly one saturated hue.
ROOT_CAUSES = focal-color ambiguity appears when another supporting mass reaches comparable chroma; increasing saturation without hierarchy can create competition rather than emphasis. Synthetic color separability cannot prove production taste/generalization, and pixel-domain palette metrics cannot infer hidden character geometry under issue #202.
REGRESSION_RESULTS = prior value-grouping lesson replay on deterministic noisy three-mass composition: OpenCV Lab-L kmeans K=3 produced class IoUs 1.000000/1.000000/1.000000 and macro-IoU 1.000000, preserving DARK/MID/LIGHT semantic separation.
TRANSFER_TEST = changed/unseen palette 22/24/31, 70/76/88, 160/154/146, focal 233/65/47: supporting C*=5.273/7.864/5.025, focal C*=79.416, focal lead 71.552, minimum Lab separation 76.627. After exposure 0.93 plus warm white-balance multipliers R/G/B=1.04/1.00/0.96, focal remained unique top chroma C*=78.940 with lead 70.386 and minimum Lab separation 73.108. Synthetic scope only.
SKILL_DELTA =
- color_accent_hierarchy_qc: UNTESTED -> PARTIAL
- value_grouping_qc: PARTIAL -> PARTIAL
- negative_space_grouping_qc: PARTIAL -> PARTIAL
SELF_MODEL_DELTA =
- CHROMA_HIERARCHY_RULE = Judge color emphasis relationally: a focal accent is useful when it remains distinctly stronger than supporting chroma, not merely because its saturation is numerically high.
- ACCENT_COMPETITION_RULE = A second high-chroma mass can destroy focal uniqueness even when both colors are individually attractive; measure top-vs-second chroma competition before adding more accents.
- COLOR_CONFIDENCE_RULE = Synthetic Lab separation is a diagnostic for hierarchy behavior, not a production taste threshold; require approved real-raster transfer before promoting the skill beyond PARTIAL.
OWNER_TASTE_SIGNALS = issue #199 explicitly orders 4-6 CONTROLLED TONE BANDS -> SPARSE ACCENT DARKS/HIGHLIGHTS -> STOP and rejects uncontrolled microdetail/noise; issue #198 makes silhouette/identity primary; issue #202 permits pixel-domain tone-band/raster QC but forbids treating pixels as physical character geometry. No new OWNER preference inferred.
OWNER_TASTE_MODEL_DELTA =
- SPARSE_ACCENT_HIERARCHY = CONFIRMED_SUPPORTING_SIGNAL only: existing OWNER law explicitly prefers sparse accents after macro silhouette/value structure; this cycle supports relational chroma hierarchy as a QC aid but does not create a universal one-accent or numeric chroma-threshold law.
ZORR_APPLICATION = Build color after silhouette and coarse value masses. Keep supporting palette chroma restrained enough that intended focal accents remain unmistakably separated; if two regions compete at similar chroma, decide deliberately which one owns attention or reduce one. Use Lab/chroma metrics as QC evidence, never as a substitute for art direction or Character Truth.
PRIME_CORE_CHANGED = NO
PRODUCTION_MUTATION = NO
CANON_MUTATION = NO
MODEL_WEIGHT_MUTATION = NO
NEXT_TARGETS = non-mutating transfer on an approved Tier-1 production raster/palette when durable bytes are available; inspect Krita/OpenColorIO ready-made palette/color-management workflows; test whether sparse accent hierarchy survives expansion from three coarse value masses into issue-#199-compliant 4-6 production tone bands without silhouette/negative-space drift.
